title: Narrative Reliability
statements: The narrator gives accurate facts but misunderstands the emotional meaning of events.
The narrator intentionally hides information to manipulate the reader.
The narrator knows the thoughts and actions of several characters.
The narration closely follows one character while remaining in third person.

title: Literary Techniques in Context
statements: A broken watch appears several times before becoming crucial evidence in the final chapter.
Readers know that the friendly visitor is the murderer, but the protagonist does not.
A detective spends half the novel investigating a suspicious neighbor who has nothing to do with the crime.
The first chapter shows the protagonist escaping a burning building before explaining how the fire began.

title: Story Structure
statements: A journalist receives an anonymous file that begins the central investigation.
Every new clue puts the journalist in greater danger and reveals a larger conspiracy.
The journalist finally confronts the person responsible and must decide whether to publish the evidence.
The final chapter shows how the investigation changed the journalist’s career and relationships.

title: Character Roles
statements: A respected commander is destroyed because pride prevents him from accepting advice.
A quiet friend exists mainly so the protagonist can reveal private fears and plans.
A cynical protagonist lies, steals, and behaves selfishly but remains the central figure of the story.
An experienced scientist trains the young protagonist before the main expedition.

title: Figurative Language
statements: “The city swallowed everyone who arrived with dreams.”
“The waiting room was as silent as an abandoned church.”
“I have explained this a million times.”
“The old staircase complained under every step.”

title: Types of Irony
statements: A fire station burns down because its alarm system fails.
A character says “What wonderful timing” after missing the final train.
Readers know there is someone hiding behind the door while the character enters the room calmly.
A novel repeatedly describes an obviously corrupt politician as “our flawless public servant.”

title: Narrative Structure
statements: Events from 1995 and 2025 alternate until their connection becomes clear.
The final scene returns to the exact railway platform where the novel began.
A traveler tells a story about another traveler, whose own story becomes the main narrative.
The novel begins after the central conflict has already started and explains earlier events later.

title: Literary Forms & Genres
statements: A novel is told entirely through emails, diary entries, and police reports.
A realistic family story contains ghosts and impossible events that everyone accepts as normal.
A novel follows a teenager’s intellectual and emotional development into adulthood.
A fictional society of animals is used to explore political power and social inequality.

title: Style & Language
statements: The author consistently uses short, abrupt sentences during dangerous scenes.
A character uses informal expressions that are typical of everyday conversation.
A lawyer speaks differently in court than when talking to a close friend.
One character has a recognizable habit of using scientific vocabulary in every conversation.

title: Meaning Beneath the Surface
statements: A dead garden repeatedly appears whenever a family relationship deteriorates.
Locked doors appear throughout a novel and reinforce its concern with emotional isolation.
The novel repeatedly explores whether personal freedom is possible without loneliness.
A white bird in one particular scene represents the protagonist’s desire to escape.

title: Ending Types
statements: The final scene allows two equally plausible explanations of what really happened.
The story ends before revealing whether the protagonist accepts an important offer.
The final revelation forces the reader to reinterpret many earlier scenes.
The story returns to its opening location, but the protagonist now views it differently.

title: Character Development
statements: A selfish character gradually becomes willing to sacrifice something important for others.
A strict teacher behaves almost exactly the same at the beginning and end of the novel.
A complex protagonist is compassionate in some situations but deeply manipulative in others.
A minor shopkeeper is defined almost entirely by constant pessimism.

title: Rhetorical Devices
statements: “We waited for answers. We waited for justice. We waited for change.”
“They demanded freedom, fought for freedom, and finally won freedom.”
“She wanted peace; he wanted victory.”
“Who could look at these results and claim nothing needs to change?”

title: Suspense & Plot Devices
statements: A chapter ends just as the detective opens the hidden safe.
A mysterious necklace motivates several characters, although its actual value is irrelevant.
A previously unknown billionaire appears in the final chapter and solves every financial problem.
Early references to unstable ice become important when a character later tries to cross the lake.

title: Identify the Narrative Technique
statements: The narration suddenly adopts the protagonist’s irritated vocabulary without saying “she thought.”
The text follows a character’s thoughts as they jump between a smell, a childhood memory, tomorrow’s meeting, and a song.
The narrator pauses to complain that the author has written the scene incorrectly.
The protagonist silently considers every possible consequence of confessing the truth.

title: Sound & Language Devices
statements: “Silver streets shimmered silently beneath the storm.”
“The low road rolled slowly home.”
“The clock went tick-tock in the empty room.”
“The black rock cracked beneath his boot.”

title: Conflict Types
statements: A climber struggles to survive a blizzard after becoming separated from the group.
A journalist must decide whether revealing the truth is worth betraying a close friend.
A teenager challenges a law that prevents certain citizens from attending university.
Two business partners compete for control of the same company.

title: Point of View
statements: “I knew the letter was a mistake, but I opened it anyway.”
“You step into the corridor and immediately notice the silence.”
“Maya watched the train leave. She wondered whether she had made the right decision.”
“Maya regretted leaving, while across town Daniel was already celebrating her departure.”

title: Literary Meaning
statements: The repeated image of empty chairs reinforces a novel’s exploration of absence.
A storm in one scene represents the collapse of a character’s emotional control.
The novel repeatedly asks whether ambition can coexist with loyalty.
A fictional kingdom represents a real political system throughout the entire story.

title: Forms of Characterization
statements: “Marcus was impatient and rarely trusted anyone.”
Marcus checks the lock three times before leaving every room.
A confident character is paired with an anxious partner to highlight their differences.
A minor character is defined almost entirely by greed.

title: Genre Recognition
statements: A detective investigates a murder inside a mansion that nobody could have entered or left.
A young woman grows from an insecure student into an independent adult over several years.
A realistic village treats conversations with ghosts as perfectly ordinary.
A politician’s absurd rise to power is used to criticize bureaucracy and corruption.

title: Narrative Time
statements: The story pauses in 2030 to show an important scene from 2002.
A chapter briefly shows the protagonist twenty years in the future.
Events are presented in the exact order in which they occur.
The novel alternates repeatedly between childhood, adulthood, and the present investigation.

title: Tone Identification
statements: The narrator describes a disaster using dry jokes and exaggerated politeness.
A childhood home is described with warmth and gentle longing.
A ruined city is presented through bleak images and hopeless observations.
A narrator mocks every decision made by a self-important politician.

title: Plot Function
statements: The protagonist learns that their employer has been secretly falsifying records.
Attempts to investigate lead to threats, lost evidence, and betrayal.
The protagonist publicly releases the evidence despite knowing the consequences.
Several months later, the company has collapsed and the protagonist begins a new career.

title: Word Meaning
statements: “Home” literally means the place where someone lives.
“Home” may suggest safety, belonging, or childhood memories.
“Passed away” is used instead of “died.”
Calling an old apartment a “dump” makes it sound deliberately unpleasant.

title: Genre Expectations
statements: A romance introduces two rivals who gradually fall in love.
A fantasy novel presents a chosen hero who immediately refuses to save the kingdom.
A detective story includes clues, suspects, and a final explanation.
A phrase such as “cold as ice” feels predictable because it has been used excessively.

title: Rhetorical Appeals
statements: “As a surgeon with thirty years of experience, I have seen the consequences firsthand.”
“The study followed 12,000 participants and found a 34% reduction in risk.”
“Imagine a child going to bed hungry every night.”
“How can we claim the system works when half the population cannot access it?”

title: Storytelling Objects
statements: A mysterious briefcase motivates every faction, although its contents are never revealed.
A rifle displayed prominently in Chapter 1 is used during the climax.
A necklace appears repeatedly and represents the protagonist’s connection to their mother.
A false diary sends the investigator toward the wrong suspect.

title: Intertextual Relationships
statements: A modern novel retells a Greek myth from the villain’s perspective.
A comedy exaggerates the conventions of detective fiction to make them ridiculous.
A new mystery lovingly imitates the tone and structure of classic 1930s crime novels.
A novel repeatedly references characters and scenes from several older literary works.

title: Character Development Analysis
statements: A cowardly soldier gradually becomes willing to risk their life for others.
A rigid judge experiences multiple crises but ends the story with exactly the same worldview.
A protagonist is compassionate, jealous, ambitious, insecure, and capable of contradictory choices.
A side character exists primarily to provide comic complaints and never develops beyond that role.

title: Difficult Narrative Interpretation
statements: A narrator insists their marriage is perfect while repeatedly describing evidence of serious conflict.
The narrator is a child who reports events accurately but cannot understand their adult significance.
Different narrators describe the same accident in contradictory ways.
The story refuses to enter anyone’s thoughts and reports only visible actions and dialogue.

title: Style Through Sentence Design
statements: The author uses fragments such as “Footsteps. Darkness. Silence.” during a chase.
The narrator consistently chooses technical medical vocabulary.
Dialogue contains informal expressions associated with one particular region.
The character speaks formally to a professor but casually to a sibling.

title: Figurative Meaning
statements: “Hope was a tiny candle refusing to go out.”
“His explanation was as clear as fog.”
“The silence screamed across the room.”
“She carried enough luggage to move an entire country.”

title: World & Setting
statements: The story takes place in 1920s Paris during a period of major social change.
The author establishes laws, currency, religion, geography, and political institutions for a fictional planet.
Fog, distant bells, and abandoned streets create a threatening emotional environment.
The repeated contrast between wealthy districts and crowded factories reinforces the story’s concern with inequality.

title: Literary Form Recognition
statements: The story consists of letters exchanged between two people over twenty years.
The narrator repeatedly discusses how difficult it is to write the novel the reader is currently reading.
Several travelers tell separate stories inside a larger journey narrative.
A fictional political revolution mirrors the structure of a real historical revolution.
